top_story: U.S. strikes on three Iranian oil tankers on 5 September, after attempted missile attacks near naval vessels, mark a sharp escalation in the Gulf and reinforce a retaliatory cycle in which Iran’s Revolutionary Guards are widening pressure on U.S.-linked shipping. Along Israel’s northern front, fresh air attacks in Arab Salim and Nabatieh al-Fawqa killed four people as Lebanon’s broader toll since 2023 approached 9,000 dead, with repeated strikes on ambulance crews and healthcare workers underscoring how routine violence is hollowing out civilian protection. The revived scrutiny of the April 2024 killing of seven World Central Kitchen staff on the road to Rafah adds to a regional pattern in which military actors continue operations despite well-known humanitarian risks and deconfliction mechanisms. The immediate picture is of interconnected fronts where retaliation logic is deepening insecurity at sea and on land, while civilians and aid networks absorb the cumulative cost.
